quarterly_data.signal: AEP's 10-Q: management forecasts approximately $12.8 billion of capital expenditures in 2026 and $65.1 billion for the four-year period 2027 through 2030, reflecting planned investments in transmission infrastructure and new generation resources to support existing customers and forecasted large load increases. The 2026-2030 budgeted capital expenditures total $77,937 million by segment, including Vertically Integrated Utilities $40,879 million, Transmission and Distribution Utilities $22,537 million and AEP Transmission Holdco $12,855 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex ~$12.8 billion; 2027-2030 capex $65.1 billion; 2026-2030 budget $77,937 million (Vertically Integrated Utilities $40,879 million, Transmission and Distribution Utilities $22,537 million, AEP Transmission Holdco $12,855 million)

quarterly_data.signal: AEP's 10-Q: its large load tariff proposals strengthen and lengthen contract terms with large load customers, including contract lengths of up to 20 years and take-or-pay contractual minimums that can require a customer to pay for as much as 80-90% of its contracted demand. As of March 31, 2026 the proposals were filed in eight AEP jurisdictions with four approved by state commissions; in the second quarter of 2026 the Virginia commission approved APCo's large load tariff, which applies to new large load additions of 150 MW or more on an aggregated basis or 100 MW or more on an individual basis; as of June 30, 2026 three proposals were pending in Michigan, Oklahoma and SWEPCo-Texas.
quarterly_data.figure: large-load contracts up to 20 years; take-or-pay minimums up to 80-90% of contracted demand; Virginia tariff threshold 150 MW aggregated / 100 MW individual
